title: Projectivity descends along faithfully flat maps
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism of commutative rings and let $M$ be an $A$-module. If $B\otimes_A M$ is projective as a $B$-module, then $M$ is projective as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-projective-module].

proof.text: Put $N=B\otimes_A M$. By [lem-trf-projective-countable-decomposition], choose a set $I$, countably generated projective $B$-modules $Q_i$ and $\theta:N\cong\bigoplus_{i\in I}Q_i$ (invert the displayed isomorphism there). By [lem-weil-pbc-well-ordering-theorem], well-order the underlying set of $M$; let $\kappa$ be its order type.

For $H\subseteq I$, let $D_H$ consist of families supported in $H$ [def-trf-coordinate-submodule], and put $T(U)=\theta(\operatorname{im}(B\otimes_A U\to N))$. Apply [lem-trf-coordinate-projective-successor] with the original faithfully flat map, the countably generated projective factors of step 1, and each $U,H,x$ with $T(U)=D_H$ and $x\notin U$. It gives $V\supseteq U$ containing $x$, with countably generated projective quotient $V/U$ and $T(V)=D_{H\cup J}$ for $J\subseteq I\setminus H$. Taking $H^{+}=H\cup J\supseteq H$ verifies the successor property in step 3.

Apply [lem-trf-coordinate-projective-exhaustion] to $\theta$, the well-order from step 1 and the successor property verified in step 2. Obtain an increasing filtration $(M_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\kappa}$ with $M_0=0$, $M_\kappa=M$, unions at every nonzero limit, and countably generated projective quotients $P_\alpha=M_{\alpha+1}/M_\alpha$ for all $\alpha<\kappa$. This includes zero quotients at any constant stages.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, recursion, limit and exhaustion paragraphs

proof.text: For every $\alpha<\kappa$, the quotient sequence $0\to M_\alpha\xrightarrow{\iota_\alpha}M_{\alpha+1}\to P_\alpha\to0$ is short exact by [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. Its quotient is projective by step 3, so [lem-weil-pbc-ses-projective-quotient-splits] supplies $r_\alpha:M_{\alpha+1}\to M_\alpha$ with $r_\alpha\circ\iota_\alpha=\mathrm{id}_{M_\alpha}$. Apply [lem-trf-split-transfinite-module-filtration] with $R=A$, $X=M$, $X_\alpha=M_\alpha$, and the set ordinal $\kappa$. Step 3 supplies the increasing family, zero initial stage, endpoint and limit unions, and these maps supply every successor retraction. Thus $M\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha<\kappa}P_\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 05A9, theorem-ffdescent-projectivity, successor splitting and final direct-sum decomposition

proof.text: Every $P_\alpha$ is projective, so [lem-weil-pbc-projective-direct-sum-family] makes $\bigoplus_{\alpha<\kappa}P_\alpha$ projective. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-direct-summand], applied to the isomorphism in step 4, gives projectivity of $M$.
